newsitem.title: USA: US stocks seen steady, eyeing data and Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: US stocks seen steady, eyeing data and Greenspan.

text.p: U.S. stocks are expected to open steady with the market awaiting another burst of economic data as well as a speech by Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan.
Banking stocks could be sparked by a merger pact between NationsBank and Boatmen's Bancshares.

"We again have a bunch of numbers coming up and depending on how it affects bonds, it'll affect stocks," said Hildegard Zagorski, analyst for Prudential Securities. "We had a big selloff yesterday and we have weak markets overseas. I would look for a lower opening initially."
On Thursday, stronger than expected economic data prompted a sell-off, with the Dow chalking up its biggest one-day point loss since mid-July.
The government reported today that U.S. personal income rose 0.1 percent in July, while consumer spending rose 0.2 percrent.
Several reports are due at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT, including the key August Chicago Purchasing Managers Index.
"It's a precursor to next week's National Association of Purchasing Management Index," Zagorski said. The Chicago Index is is expected to rise slightly to 51.9.
